// record: an embedded record's fields promote through the outer type
// and flatten in the json output, and a flat declared struct passes by
// value into a host binding whose parameter is a named type no bound
// constructor builds: reflect's structural assignability.
type Endpoint struct {
	Host string `json:"host"`
	Port int64  `json:"port"`
}
type Server struct {
	Endpoint
	Name string `json:"name"`
}
s := Server{Endpoint: Endpoint{Host: "example.com", Port: 8080}, Name: "edge"};
assert.Equal(tb, "example.com", s.Host);
assert.Equal(tb, 8080, s.Port);

// A promoted name writes through to the embedded field it names.
var w Server;
w.Host = "db.local";
w.Port = 5432;
assert.Equal(tb, "db.local", w.Host);
assert.Equal(tb, "db.local", w.Endpoint.Host);

// The embedded fields flatten into the enclosing object.
buf := bytes.NewBufferString("");
json.NewEncoder(buf).Encode(s);
assert.Equal(tb, "{\"host\":\"example.com\",\"port\":8080,\"name\":\"edge\"}\n", buf.String());

// Session matches session.Format's parameter field for field; the host
// never bound a constructor for that type, and the value still arrives.
type Session struct {
	User string
	Host string
	Port int64
}
c := Session{User: "ana", Host: "db.local", Port: 5432};
line := session.Format(c);
assert.Equal(tb, "ana@db.local:5432", line);
